payload.title: seed_drift_findings.run_fresh_scan runs poc.py with check=True and captured output and handles nothing, so the named FileNotFoundError or ValueError that detect_sql_enums now raises for an unreadable registry reaches the operator as a bare CalledProcessError and the closure recheck records only detector_exit_1
evidence: tools/aria-poc/seed_drift_findings.py:147-161 (subprocess.run with check=True and capture_output=True, no handler; the scanner's stderr stays inside the exception)
tools/aria-poc/poc.py:946-969 (detect_sql_enums reads the registry first and raises before any scan output)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/finding_closure.py:122-124 (the recheck path reduces any non-zero exit to detector_exit_N)
tools/aria-poc/invariants/test_poc_sql_enum_visibility.py:282-309 (pins the named errors at detect_sql_enums only; nothing pins what the seeder shows)
payload.rule_violated: CLAUDE.md Working Style: report faithfully; a refusal designed to be named must reach the operator by name
payload.notes: A recheck tree with no apps/db-migrate/src/schema-registry.ts, or a registry with glob syntax the reader refuses, makes poc.py exit 1 with the cause on stderr. The seeder re-raises CalledProcessError, whose text omits stderr, so the operator sees 'returned non-zero exit status 1' and the closure recheck stores detector_exit_1 as the reason. Reachable only through a registry the reader cannot read: every historical version of schema-registry.ts uses supported globs and the real-repo tests run on every pull request, so no current run is affected. Close condition: In run_fresh_scan catch CalledProcessError and re-raise (or return a named unverifiable result) with the scanner's last stderr lines included; closed when a test with a workspace lacking the registry shows 'schema-registry.ts' in the seeder's error text. Plan row: DET detector program (landing batch 2b). Verified at head b2259fe03f of open pull request #2151; the cited code is not on main until that pull request merges.
